items.title: DAP's Anthony Loke accuses rivals of smear campaign during Negeri Sembilan polls
items.summary: JELEBU, July 30 — DAP secretary-general Loke Siew Fook has accused his political opponents of mounting a smear campaign against him during the Negri Sembilan election campaign, including claims that he would be appointed menteri besar if Pakatan Harapan (PH) wins, according to a report by Free Malaysia Today (FMT). FMT reported that Loke, who is defending the Chennah seat for PH, said baseless claims had been spread in villages to frighten Malay voters, including allegations that Malays would lose their political power if the coalition won Saturday’s election. FMT reported that during the campaign, Umno secretary-general Datuk Seri Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki had questioned whether Loke would be nominated as PH’s menteri besar candidate if former menteri besar Aminuddin Harun lost in the state election, and whether the people would accept such a nomination.

items.title: Zahid says Tabung Haji RCI review should cover recovery period too
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 30 — The Cabinet has proposed that the review period for the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) be extended to include the period of transition following the institution’s takeover by the new management. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the move would allow the recovery measures undertaken after the investigation period to be assessed. Ahmad Zahid, who is also the Rural and Regional Development Minister, said the Cabinet had also agreed for the RCI Report to be made public and tabled at a special Parliament sitting for debate.

items.title: Scammer posing as cop swindles woman of RM170,000
items.summary: District police chief Superintendent Roslan Mohd Talib said the 51-year-old woman received a call from the suspect at 10.24am on July 8 and was told she was linked to illegal activities. Roslan said the suspect then tricked the victim into making payments purportedly for investigation purposes. He said the victim eventually realised she had been scammed and lodged a report at the Tangkak district police headquarters yesterday.

items.title: 30-year yields hit 19-year highs amid Fed doubts
items.summary: SYDNEY: Yields on the US long bond hovered near 19-year highs in Asia on Thursday as markets questioned the Federal Reserve's resolve towards controlling inflation, leaving investors seeking more insurance against inflation risks. The sudden sell-off came after the Fed left rates unchanged at Wednesday's policy meeting, even as three members of the Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted for an immediate hike. The hawkish market view contrasted with Warsh's tone.

items.title: Anwar says special sitting needed for open debate on Tabung Haji report
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 30 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has proposed holding a special Parliament sitting to discuss the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) as soon as possible. He said the date, however, would need the approval of Dewan Rakyat speaker Tan Sri Dr Johari Abdul. He said the report would also be tabled and debated during a special Dewan Rakyat sitting soon.

items.title: 'I'm like Sivaji the Boss,' Anwar says in Negri ceramah
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has likened his political journey to the Tamil action film "Sivaji: The Boss", recounting how he overcame imprisonment and setbacks before becoming prime minister. The Pakatan Harapan chairman drew the comparison during a meet-and-greet session with the Indian community here last night, recalling his early struggles when founding PKR. Separately, Anwar announced that he will personally oversee all issues concerning the Indian community immediately, with the help of PKR vice-president Datuk Seri R. Ramanan.

items.title: Starbucks raises annual forecasts again as turnaround takes root
items.summary: Under Niccol, the company has aimed to improve customer experience through a simplified menu and shortened wait times, fueling four straight quarters of comparable sales growth. "We have more work to do," Niccol said in a statement on Wednesday, while finance chief Cathy Smith said the company is focused on what it can control amid a "dynamic operating environment" The Seattle-based company forecast global same-store sales growth of near 6 per cent, above its prior forecast of about 5 per cent or above. It expects adjusted earnings per share to be between US$2.55 and US$2.65, compared with its previous forecast of US$2.25 to US$2.45.

items.title: Why Cash Flow Is King when Investing
items.summary: The famous investing maxim "Cash is king" reflects a simple truth: companies survive, grow, and reward shareholders with cash - not accounting profits. Cash flow refers to the actual movement of cash into and out of a business. For long-term investors, cash flow often provides a clearer picture of business quality than earnings alone.

items.title: Chinese carmakers piling pressure on UK rivals, auto industry chief says
items.summary: LONDON: A wave of Chinese entrants into Britain's car market is piling pressure on traditional manufacturers, forcing them to offer deeper discounts to compete with lower-cost imports, the head of the country's main automotive industry body said on Thursday. Chinese brands have rapidly expanded their presence in Britain in recent years, winning market share with competitively priced electric and plug-in hybrid models and intensifying competition for established automakers. Last week, Germany's Volkswagen said it would deepen cost cuts to remain competitive against Chinese brands.

items.title: Salman Rushdie stabbing: Assailant convicted of terrorism, faces life sentence
items.summary: NEW YORK: A federal jury on Wednesday convicted novelist Salman Rushdie's assailant of "engaging in an act of terrorism" for the bloody August 2022 attack at a New York cultural centre. Hadi Matar, a 28-year-old Lebanese American, "chose to align his values with the terroristic values of the leaders of Iran," said US Attorney Michael DiGiacomo, adding the defendant spent months planning the stabbing that nearly killed Rushdie and left him blind in one eye. Federal prosecutors said Matar followed a fatwa calling for Rushdie's execution, first issued in 1989 by the late Iranian leader Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini, for fictionalising the Prophet Muhammad in his bestselling book, "The Satanic Verses."

items.title: Wall Street closes down sharply after Fed holds rates unchanged
items.summary: NEW YORK: Wall Street ended sharply lower on Wednesday after the Federal Reserve held interest rates steady, with AI-related chip stocks adding to recent declines ahead of quarterly reports from Microsoft and Meta Platforms and the Nasdaq 100 index marking an 11 per cent drop from its June record high. The benchmark S&P 500 hit its lowest level in a month, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite index was down about 9 per cent from its June record high. The Nasdaq 100 index dropped 2.1 per cent, extending recent losses as investors unloaded AI-related stocks due to ongoing concerns about heavy capital spending.

items.title: Bolivia prosecutor orders arrest of ex-leader Morales over protests
items.summary: LA PAZ, (Bolivia): Bolivian prosecutors on Wednesday issued an arrest warrant for former socialist president Evo Morales, accusing him of fomenting recent protests that paralysed the country. But protests escalated to demand the resignation of US-backed President Rodrigo Paz, who has accused Morales of orchestrating the unrest. Morales denies the allegations.

items.title: New corporate champions, new-age banking
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia risks struggling to produce its next generation of corporate champions unless the financial sector takes a more forward-looking approach to risk, innovation and entrepreneurship, industry leaders said. At the same time, Islamic banks risk losing relevance among younger customers if they fail to match expectations for seamless, customer-focused digital banking. Nothing much has changed," he said.

items.title: Maju Junction assets up for auction with RM353.95mil reserve price
items.summary: The auction follows execution proceedings involving Perwaja Terengganu Sdn Bhd as plaintiff and ASM Properties as defendant, according to the proclamation of sale issued by the High Court of Malaya here. On July 25, 2019, the High Court entered judgment in favour of Perwaja, ordering Maju Holdings to pay RM197.99 million, together with interest. Maju Holdings subsequently appealed, but the Court of Appeal dismissed the appeal on Dec 20, 2022, upholding the High Court's decision.

items.title: Affordable housing vital for long-term economic stability
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Affordable housing programmes are more than a way to bridge the housing affordability gap— they also help young Malaysians build wealth, improve social mobility and achieve long-term economic stability. Universiti Teknologi Malaysia Associate Professor (property economics) Dr Muhammad Najib Razali said state housing schemes such as Rumah Selangorku help address market gaps, as private developers often focus on higher-profit segments beyond the reach of many low- and middle-income households. Najib said such programmes promoted community stability and sustainable urban growth .

items.title: Putrajaya wants federal, state housing schemes to complement each other
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Putrajaya aims to create an ecosystem where federal and state affordable housing schemes complement rather than compete with one another. The government said raising the homeownership rate would require a coordinated approach combining affordable housing supply, easier financing, policy reforms and closer collaboration among the federal and state governments, financial institutions and the private sector. Deputy Housing and Local Government Minister Datuk Aiman Athirah Sabu said this approach would enable more Malaysians to buy homes that matched their preferred location, budget and financial capacity.

items.title: Homeownership: Opening doors for young Malaysians
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Soaring property prices and the rising cost of living have pushed homeownership beyond the reach of many young Malaysians. The sales manager, who earns about RM6,000 monthly, said the affordable pricing for the partially furnished apartment made the scheme an attractive option. The affordable housing scheme helped me achieve that goal without placing too much financial pressure on me," she said.

items.title: Negri Sembilan polls: Status quo tested as race heats up
items.summary: Following BN's commanding performance in Johor and the perceived weakening of Pakatan Harapan in several rural and semi-urban constituencies, political momentum appears to be shifting. Although DAP continues to retain several established strong-holds, recent political trends are widely interpreted by BN-PN supporters as fractures in PH's support that could be strategically exploited. PH secured 17 seats, including all 11 contested by DAP, while BN won 14 seats and PN obtained five.

items.title: Firefighting helicopter crash kills seven in Argentina
items.summary: BUENOS AIRES: Seven people died when a firefighting helicopter in Argentina's western San Juan province crashed on Wednesday, a local official said. It lost contact with base on Wednesday morning at around 10.30 am (1330 GMT). "With profound sorrow, we received the news of the helicopter accident that occurred in our province, in which seven people sadly lost their lives," San Juan Governor Marcelo Orrego wrote on X. Fatalities included firefighters, police officers and civil protection personnel, he said.

items.title: MyIMMs breach a national security issue, not just cybercrime, says criminologist [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The alleged hacking and manipulation of the Malaysian Immigration System (MyIMMs) should be treated as a national security issue rather than merely a corruption or cybercrime case. Senior criminologist Datuk Dr P. Sundramoorthy said the Immigration Department serves as Malaysia's first line of defence, making any compromise of the MyIMMs platform a direct threat to the country's border security and sovereignty. Sundramoorthy said the case also highlighted the dangerous convergence between organised crime and insider corruption, noting that criminal syndicates rarely succeed without assistance from individuals entrusted with legitimate authority and system access.

items.title: This changes things: New government rules that might impact your daily life in Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 30 — From ATM withdrawals to passport renewals, and even how they buy household appliances, Malaysians are now seeing a series of changes that affects their daily routines — including how they pay for fuel or access government services. Some measures have already taken effect, while others are proposed reforms aimed at tightening enforcement, reducing subsidy leakages and pushing more services online. Here are some of the changes that could affect Malaysians' daily lives.

items.title: In Malaysia’s durian country, pomelos are quietly taking root
items.summary: JELEBU, July 30 — When Jelebu in Negeri Sembilan is mentioned, many immediately think of its lush durian orchards nestled among rolling hills and valleys. Jelebu Mardi manager Noraimi Nordin says pomelos offer farmers a lower-maintenance alternative to durians, with year-round production and strong commercial potential. — Bernama pic Jelebu Mardi manager Noraimi Nordin said pomelos have several advantages over many other crops, including lower maintenance requirements, minimal pest problems, and the ability to produce fruit year-round.

items.title: Death toll rises to 13 as rescuers search Japan quake rubble
items.summary: KUMAMOTO: Rescuers battled through the tangled wreckage of a Japanese shopping mall Wednesday searching for any trapped survivors after a strong earthquake killed at least 13 people. A massive explosion ripped through the mall around 50 minutes after the 7.1-magnitude tremor on Tuesday in the southwestern Kumamoto region, where in 2016 twin quakes killed nearly 300 people. Akio Yoshida, the president of mall operator Aeon, said three people died at the facility in the town of Kashima, with one more fatality feared and three others missing.

items.title: Microsoft tops forecasts as cloud, AI drive US$90b revenue
items.summary: The tech giant reported US$90 billion in revenue and US$35.8 billion in net income in the last quarter of its fiscal year which ended in June, potentially alleviating concerns from investors and analysts about whether its investments in AI are paying off. Microsoft also saw a US$3.2 billion gain from its investment in Anthropic, the company said. Its investments in OpenAI boosted Microsoft's net profit by US$480 million in its fourth quarter and US$4.9 billion for its full fiscal year, the company added.

items.title: Thousands return home in Spain as new heatwave fuels France wildfires
items.summary: ALDEA DEL FRESNO, Spain: Thousands who fled huge wildfires in Spain returned home on Wednesday while in France firefighters battled raging flames as a new heatwave gripped the region. Spain lifted remaining evacuation orders for Avila province and for the last two towns near Madrid that had been evacuated on Wednesday. Officials said on Wednesday that better overnight conditions had helped crews stabilise the fire area, and Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said the coming hours would be "decisive" in the battle to extinguish all the remaining flames.

items.title: Trump vows to hit Iran hard after attack on US bases in Jordan
items.summary: Teheran: US President Donald Trump vowed to hit back hard at Iran after it attacked US bases in Jordan on Wednesday, as the Middle East war reignited and again drew in the Islamic republic's proxies. On Wednesday, Saudi Arabia and the United States announced strikes on militant bases in Iraq, while US ally Israel accused Iran-backed Hizbollah of a truce violation. Iran meanwhile launched missiles at US ally Jordan, with Iranian state media later reporting an American attack near the Islamic republic's border with Iraq.

items.title: Meta profit falls 14pct as AI spending climbs to US$145bil
items.summary: The social media giant said net income dropped 14 per cent from a year earlier to US$15.8 billion. Revenue, however, climbed 28 per cent to US$60.8 billion, beating estimates and underscoring the continued strength of its advertising business. At Meta, the profit decline was driven largely by one-time items, including US$2.4 billion in charges tied to legal proceedings and US$1.2 billion in severance from a round of layoffs in May.

items.title: Pantun contest returns for 2nd year
items.summary: Following the success of its inaugural edition last year, the Pertandingan Pantun Bertemakan Peribahasa DRB-HICOM Bersama Harian Metro is returning for a second year. DRB-HICOM chief communications officer Cairil Irwan Amir said the competition was organised following the encouraging response to its inaugural edition in Selangor last year. "Last year's pantun competition received a very good response.

items.title: HBA: 'No deposit' still carries financial burden
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Affordable housing schemes should not only help Malaysians buy their first home but also ensure they can comfortably repay their loans over the long term. National House Buyers Association (HBA) secretary-general Datuk Chang Kim Loong said schemes such as Rumah Selangorku and Rumah Mampu Milik had helped first-time buyers overcome one of the biggest barriers — raising the upfront 10 per cent deposit. Chang said saving for a deposit would foster a buyer's financial discipline, reflecting their commitment to homeownership.

items.title: Top earners make six times more
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The top 10 per cent of formal sector employees earned at least RM11,500 a month in March 2026, more than six times the wages of the country's lowest-paid workers. The number of formal workers rose 3.8 per cent year-on-year to 7.05 million in March 2026. Workers aged 45 to 49 earned the highest median wages, ranging from RM4,100 to RM4,156 in the first quarter.

items.title: 'Crackdown undermines law'
items.summary: SYDNEY: Elon Musk's X has accused Australia of trying to give its Internet regulator unfair information-gathering powers and undermining United States law with plans for tougher enforcement of a teen social media ban. Australia's world-first law barring accounts for under-16s took effect last December, drawing criticism from social media companies, mostly based in the US. The plans did not give "due regard to procedural fairness, privacy, the broader impacts on online services, and Australia's digital economy", X told an Australian senate committee.

items.title: ASML faces competition from China's homegrown chip tool technology
items.summary: CHINA'S launch of a homegrown type of advanced lithography chip printing machine is spotlighting how European chip tool maker ASML, whose recent share price surge made it Europe's most valuable listed company, is being squeezed between two sides. ASML has a dominant position in the market for lithography tools, including its mid-range DUV devices. The Information said China plans to make five immersion DUV tools this year and 20 in 2027, selling them to major Chinese chipmakers.

items.title: Israel's 'yellow line' pushing Gazans from home
items.summary: ON a road in Gaza City's Zeitoun district, Palestinian resident Assem Dawla loaded mattresses and bags onto a truck as concrete yellow blocks marking the edge of Israel's expanding military zone stood amid the rubble nearby. Continued Israeli military activity made it too dangerous to remain, Dawla said. Israeli forces have continued near-daily military strikes across Gaza.

items.title: NST Leader: Migrants and refugees causing concern
items.summary: The World Bank and International Organisation for Migration estimates that for a populace of between 1.2 million and 3.5 million, for every 10 legal migrants, there will be seven to 10 undocumented ones. Think tanks say the numbers may be even larger: 3.8 million and 5.5 million in legal and illegal workers, respectively. Despite Malaysia's decades-long effort to contain them, undocumented migrants keep turning up on our doorsteps.

items.title: NS Polls: Loke says support momentum for PH at its strongest level
items.summary: DAP secretary-general and Negri Sembilan chairman Anthony Loke said PH had consistently explained its achievements, service record and manifesto pledges to voters throughout the campaign. He said attempts by certain quarters to exploit defamatory political narratives, including linking DAP to the Negri Sembilan Palace to intimidate Malay voters, had backfired after the palace issued an official statement. Also present were Prime Minister and PH chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, Amanah president Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu, his deputy Datuk Seri Dr Mujahid Yusof Rawa, and PH candidates contesting the state election.

items.title: National Trust Fund’s net assets expected to double within 10 years, Dewan Negara told
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 29 — Consistent inflows into the National Trust Fund (KWAN), including accumulated investment returns, are expected to double the fund’s net assets in about 10 years, according to Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong. He said the annual inflows, estimated at nearly RM800 million, would include at least 0.1 per cent of the projected annual revenue of the government revenue, or about RM343 million based on Budget 2026 estimates. “The contributions must be transferred into the fund before the end of the relevant financial year.

items.title: MCMC busts fake mobile tower SMS scam syndicate in Johor Bahru
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, July 29 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has busted a syndicate using a fake base transceiver station (BTS) to send fraudulent short message service (SMS) messages containing scam links to the public. In a statement, MCMC said that during an operation in Johor Bahru last Friday, a 32-year-old local man was found driving a vehicle equipped with a fake BTS device that transmitted radio signals to send fraudulent SMS messages containing website links while impersonating a telecommunications service provider. A fake BTS is a non-compliant communications device that mimics mobile network signals, enabling SMS messages to be sent directly to users’ mobile phones without passing through the official network of a telecommunications service provider, making scam or spoofed messages appear legitimate.

items.title: MoF: RON97, unsubsidised RON95 and diesel prices up 20 sen a litre from July 30 to Aug 5
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 29 — The retail prices of RON97, unsubsidised RON95 and unsubsidised diesel will each increase by 20 sen per litre for the period from July 30 to August 5. The price of unsubsidised diesel will also increase to RM4.62 per litre from RM4.42. Meanwhile, the ministry said subsidised fuel prices for the period from July 30 to August 5 remain unchanged.

items.title: Businessman loses appeal against conviction for threatening and assaulting bodyguards in Klang
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, July 29 — The High Court here today upheld the prison sentence against a businessman who was found guilty of three charges involving threats, causing hurt, and insulting two of his bodyguards in 2021. Judge Datuk Seri Shamsulbahri Ibrahim ordered that the five-year prison sentence against Chung Chee Yang, 48, commence today, after dismissing the appeal against conviction and sentence on 14 grounds of appeal. In conclusion, I dismiss the appeal against conviction and sentence.

items.title: Zahid backs police investigation into alleged vote-buying ahead of Negeri Sembilan poll
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 29 — The practice of offering bribes to voters during the 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election campaign must be rejected and should not be allowed to occur, said Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. Also present were Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir and Majlis Amanah Rakyat (MARA) chairman Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki. Meanwhile, Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said three investigation papers were opened yesterday, bringing the total number of investigation papers opened by police for election offences since campaigning for the 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election began on July 18 to 19.

items.title: Anwar says Myanmar agrees to accept 5,000 Rohingya refugees from Malaysia
items.summary: JELEBU, July 29 — Myanmar has agreed to take in about 5,000 Rohingya refugees currently in Malaysia, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. “People ask to send them back (the Rohingya refugees), but send them back where? He reiterated that Rohingya refugees in Malaysia must not disrupt public order by gathering on roads or at public places.

items.title: Police adopt ‘Record now, arrest later’ approach ahead of RXZ motorcycle gathering in Terengganu
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 29 — Police have warned participants of the upcoming RXZ Members gathering that anyone performing dangerous stunts or violating traffic laws will be arrested at home. Bukit Aman Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department (JSPT) director Datuk Seri Muhammed Hasbullah Ali said police are working with the organisers this year to spread safety messages through an advisory approach. However, he said this approach does not mean police will be lenient in enforcing the law against repeat offenders.

items.title: Bukit Aman arrests suspended officer alleged to be behind RM21.3m Cheras drug-trafficking ring
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 29 — Police have crippled a drug trafficking syndicate after seizing 425.3 kilogrammes of methamphetamine worth an estimated RM21.3 million in operations in Cheras, near here. Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the syndicate’s suspected mastermind and five other men aged between 39 and 46 were also arrested in the operations conducted from last Saturday until yesterday. He said police had also identified the remaining members of the syndicate and would take aggressive action to eradicate their drug distribution activities.

items.title: Appeal Court pauses contempt proceedings over Negeri Sembilan constitutional dispute
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, July 29 — The Court of Appeal today allowed a stay of committal proceedings against six individuals, pending the hearing and disposal of their appeal against the Seremban High Court’s decision granting leave for those proceedings to be initiated. The committal proceedings arise from allegations that the six individuals had breached an ad interim injunction order issued by the High Court on June 5. The six are former Undang Luak Sungai Ujong Datuk Mubarak Thahak, Undang Luak Jelebu Datuk Maarof Mat Rashad, Undang Luak Johol Datuk Muhammed Abdullah, Undang Luak Rembau Datuk Abdul Rahim Yasin, Tunku Besar Tampin Tunku Syed Razman Tunku Syed Idrus Al-Qadri, and Shahbandar Sungai Ujong Datuk Seri Badarudin Abdul Khalid.

items.title: Federal Court rejects Rosmah’s bid to review judge recusal ruling in solar hybrid graft case
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, July 29 — The Federal Court today dismissed Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor’s application to review the apex court’s earlier decision dismissing her appeal to recuse Justice Datuk Mohamed Zaini Mazlan, the judge who had presided over her RM1.25 billion solar hybrid project corruption case and convicted her in 2022. Therefore, the application for review is dismissed,” said Justice Azizah, who sat with Federal Court Judges Datuk Lee Swee Seng and Datuk Ravinthran N. Paramaguru. Rosmah’s recusal application was dismissed by the High Court on September 1, 2022, and her appeal was also rejected by the Court of Appeal on September 17 last year.

items.title: ‘If there is evidence, they will be charged’: Anwar pledges action after Tabung Haji RCI report release
items.summary: JELEBU, July 29 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today stressed that any individual found responsible for losses suffered by Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), based on the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report released today, will be brought to justice. He said any elements of misappropriation, fraud and abuse of power identified in the report would be thoroughly investigated by the relevant authorities, including the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) and Bank Negara Malaysia. “Those responsible for the losses, fraud and abuse of power will be investigated by the police, the MACC and Bank Negara... everyone will be investigated.

items.title: Demolition of Sungai Pari Flats rests with appointed developer, says LPHP CEO
items.summary: IPOH, July 29 — The decision on when the long-abandoned Sungai Pari Flats in Buntong will be demolished, and who will carry out the work, rests entirely with the appointed developer, Perak Housing and Property Board (LPHP) chief executive officer Zaiteena Wan Nasir said. Two teenage girls were recently found dead at the flats. The developer is prioritising safety at the site,” she said.

items.title: Fahmi: Pakatan plans 24-hour TikTok livestream to reach young Negeri Sembilan voters
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 29 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) will intensify its campaign efforts, including holding a continuous TikTok livestream for more than 24 hours to engage young voters ahead of polling day for the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election this Saturday. PH Communications Director Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said all PH candidates will continue working to secure victory for the coalition, including winning all 16 seats contested by PKR to strengthen PH’s overall performance in the election. He said this after visiting the Negeri Sembilan bureau of the Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama), accompanied by Communications Ministry secretary-general Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah and Bernama Editor-in-Chief Arul Rajoo Durar Raj.

items.title: Selangor plans support for 400 workers affected by Panasonic factory closure
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, July 29 — The Selangor state government is expected to receive detailed information tomorrow regarding the fate of approximately 400 workers affected by the closure of the television production plant by Panasonic AVC Networks Kuala Lumpur Malaysia Sdn Bhd (PAVCKM) here. Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said that the measure would enable appropriate forms of intervention to be implemented through the cooperation of the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) and the Selangor Labour Department (JTK). Previously, Panasonic Malaysia Sdn.

items.title: Bukit Aman busts three drug-laced vape syndicates after students fall ill in Sentul
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 29 — Police have busted three syndicates involved in the distribution of vape liquids containing synthetic drugs in separate operations across the Klang Valley last Thursday and Saturday. He said that under Op Kesing, Op Madarini and Op Eristalis, police arrested eight men, including two foreign nationals, and six foreign women, aged between 20 and 55, who are believed to be involved in the three syndicates. Police also seized various types of drugs estimated to be worth RM45.6 million.

items.title: Appeal Court upholds stay on compensation for families of missing pastor Raymond Koh and activist Amri Che Mat
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, July 29 — The Court of Appeal today upheld the High Court’s decision to stay the execution of a RM37 million damages award to the family of missing pastor Raymond Koh, as well as a RM3 million award to the family of missing activist Amri Che Mat, pending the disposal of the government’s appeals. A three-member bench comprising Justices Datuk Dr Alwi Abdul Wahab, Datuk Dr Shahnaz Sulaiman, and Datuk Amarjeet Singh unanimously dismissed the appeals filed by Koh’s wife, Susanna Liew Sow Yoke, and Amri’s wife, Norhayati Ariffin, challenging the Kuala Lumpur High Court’s stay order. In delivering the judgment, Justice Alwi stated that the High Court judge had correctly applied the established principles governing the grant of a stay.

items.title: Special Dewan Rakyat sitting needed for MPs to scrutinise Tabung Haji RCI report, says Fahmi
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 29 — The government hopes to hold a special Dewan Rakyat sitting soon to debate the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), as it is an important issue that requires scrutiny by Members of Parliament. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had asked Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said to liaise with Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul to determine the date for the special sitting. Elaborating, Fahmi said today’s Cabinet meeting was briefed by TH chairman and RCI member Tan Sri Abdul Rashid Hussain on the findings of the inquiry.

items.title: Selangor JPJ seizes 34 vehicles in crackdown on unlicensed foreign drivers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 29 — The Selangor Road Transport Department (JPJ) seized 34 vehicles in a joint operation with the Selayang Municipal Council (MPS) targeting foreign drivers this morning. Selangor JPJ director Datuk Ahmad Kamarunzaman Menhat said 126 vehicles were checked during the operation, which began at 6.30am. The operation in Selayang involved 55 JPJ officers and personnel, supported by 25 MPS officers.

items.title: Fahmi says PAS is using fear over Malay representation in Negeri Sembilan campaign
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 29 — The claim that Pakatan Harapan (PH)’s victory in the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election will lead to the redelineation of the State Legislative Assembly constituencies, thus reducing Malay and Muslim power, is an unhealthy campaign that is trying to scare the people. He said this when commenting on claims by PAS secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan that PH’s victory in Negeri Sembilan has the potential to change the state’s political landscape through an increase in the number of state assembly seats. Takiyuddin reportedly said that the state assembly constituencies that have a large number of voters and is currently represented by PH is likely to be split into several new constituencies in the future.

items.title: CAAM urges West Asia-bound passengers to check flights as airlines suspend, reroute services
items.summary: CAAM, in a statement today, said airlines may reroute flights, revise schedules or cancel certain services, and these operational adjustments may result in longer flight times, delays or disruptions to connecting flights. It said several airlines have announced temporary suspensions, cancellations or adjustments to services involving destinations in West Asia. CAAM said Malaysia Airlines’ Kuala Lumpur-Doha flight is operating daily while other Doha services are suspended until Oct 24.

items.title: Bukit Aman steps up roadblocks, but Malaysia’s drunk driving arrests barely increase
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 29 — Traffic police made over 900 arrests for drunk or intoxicated driving between January and June this year, just marginally higher than the same period last year, despite a nearly threefold increase in enforcement operations. Individuals aged 41 and above recorded the highest number of arrests, at 364 people or 38.4 per cent of total arrests by age group. Arrests involving 16 to 20 years old totalled seven people, or 0.7 per cent.

items.title: Anwar calls for massive investment, regional cooperation to drive Asean energy transition
items.summary: He said achieving the energy transition at scale would require unprecedented collaboration among the public sector, private investors and project developers to mobilise the financing needed. “It is central to strengthening Malaysia and the region’s energy security. Anwar also said that energy transition does not proceed on a straight line, nor can integration proceed in isolation.

items.title: Prasarana targets 1.7m daily riders by 2027, says 377,000 vehicles kept off roads in 2025
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 29 — Prasarana Malaysia Berhad (Prasarana) is aiming to increase its average daily ridership to 1.7 million passengers by 2027 by improving the reliability and availability of its rail and bus services, while encouraging more people to shift away from private vehicles. Prasarana Group Chairman Tan Sri Mohd Nasir Ahmad said the target is based on the company’s encouraging performance, having recorded an average of 1.3 million passenger trips per day last year. He said Prasarana would continue prioritising service reliability and availability to ensure its trains and buses remain the preferred mode of transport for commuters.

items.title: Tabung Haji welcomes RCI report release, but says it has ‘already moved on’
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 29 — Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) has embraced the government’s decision to release the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report to the public, asserting that it has already addressed the commission’s findings on events prior to 2018 and has “since moved on.” In a statement issued today, the pilgrims’ fund board revealed that it has already implemented 75 per cent of the RCI’s recommendations. Crucially, the government has also ordered enforcement agencies to launch immediate investigations into the report’s findings to ensure any lawbreakers are brought to justice. The release of the report ends a period of strategic secrecy.

items.title: Cabinet agrees to extend Act 672 to all 12 Selangor local authorities
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, July 29 — The Cabinet has agreed to extend the application of the Solid Waste and Public Cleansing Management Act 2007 (Act 672) to Selangor on a phased basis, covering all 12 local authorities in the state, said Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming. Nga added that, in line with the Cabinet decision and the National Public Cleansing Policy, the Madani government is committed to implementing public cleansing reforms under the 13th Malaysia Plan. Nga also said that waste collection and cleansing operations will shift to nighttime schedules.
